items.q: What should you remember about **Status checks ≠ context dumps**?
items.a: **leaders asking "are we on track?"** want one sentence, not every wireframe delay; over-detail reads as unclear, not thorough.

items.q: What should you remember about **Rough draft vs final version**?
items.a: **verbalizing your thinking is fine in brainstorming;** in decision moments it costs credibility ("show your work" training backfires in leadership comms).

items.q: What should you remember about **Flexibility ≠ neutrality**?
items.a: **agreeable "I don't mind" feels** safe but signals lack of decisiveness; people stop asking for your opinion.

items.q: What should you remember about **Match before you lead**?
items.a: **rapport requires mirroring first; only** then gradually shift volume, warmth, and melody to guide the room.

items.q: What should you remember about **Voice dials are learnable**?
items.a: **rate (passion vs weight), volume** (confidence vs lean-in), melody (engagement); most people play the same five keys.
